source_sections.title: The quay
source_sections.markdown:
At dusk Mara reached the quay with a letter she had promised not to read.
The ferryman was called Leno. He looked once at the letter, and then at the river.

“There's still time to go back,” he said.

Mara put one foot into the boat. Behind her, a bell sounded from the town.

source_sections.title: The crossing
source_sections.markdown:
Leno steered into the mist. Mara asked whether the far bank had a name.

“Every place has a name,” he said. “Not every traveler needs to know it.”

The letter remained unopened in her pocket.

sections.title: The quay
sections.markdown:
By the time Mara reached the quay, the light was fading. In her pocket was a
letter she had promised not to open.

The ferryman, Leno, glanced at the letter and then at the river. “There's still
time to go back,” he said.

Mara stepped into the boat. A bell rang behind her, somewhere in the town.
